note: Graph cases shared by the Python and JS ports. Generated by an independent script (recursive DFS, layer-by-layer BFS, brute-force path enumeration), NOT by dsdk.graph. Conventions: node order = the 'nodes' list; neighbours in node order; BFS parent = first discoverer; DFS = recursive preorder/postorder with roots in node order; find_cycle = first back edge in DFS order, cycle (v0..vk) with vk==v0; topological = Kahn with smallest-index-first; components/SCCs sorted canonically (nodes in node order, components by first node). Edges are [u, v] or [u, v, evidence] with evidence in known|unknown|not_observed. Undirected cases list each edge once. 'dangling_edges' reference a node that is NOT declared: building the graph with them must raise MissingNodeError. 'reachability' rows are the exact Judgment (status, value, reason) of reachable(g, source, target), including source='ghost' (a missing node => status 'invalid').

cases.name: curriculum_8
cases.description: 8 declared nodes; a 3-cycle A-B-C with a tail, a second source F, isolated node H, and a dangling reference E->Z that must raise MissingNodeError unless Z is declared.

cases.name: dag_many_orders
cases.description: DAG with many valid topological orders; Kahn's smallest-index tie-break picks one. f is isolated.

cases.name: diamond_directed
cases.description: Two equal-length routes a->d; tie-break goes through b.

cases.name: disconnected_undirected
cases.description: Two components, an isolated node f, and a self-loop on g.
